newsitem.title: POLAND: Good CPI,foreign interest to boost Polish T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Good CPI,foreign interest to boost Polish T-bills.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to continue a month-long easing at Monday's 1.3 billion zloty auction amid strong demand stirred up by good fundamentals and foreign investor interest, dealers said on Friday.
Dealers said investor bids could total about two billion zlotys on Monday, with market focus mainly on the shortest 13-week and longest 52-week bills.

"It's a good time to buy 52-week bills as inflation figures are encouraging and corporates are interested in 13-week bills, whose yields are higher than comparable deposits," said Wojciech Labryga, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
On Thursday, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) released April inflation figures showing year-on-year price growth down to 15.3 percent last month from 16.6 percent in March.

Analysts said that any talk of an interest rate cut before the third quarter was premature because credit action growth, the main concern of the central bank, remains strong despite a tight monetary policy.
Credit to the non-financial sector surged 11.6 percent in the January-April period, against a 6.7 percent increase in broad money supply.
"Last month's upbeat CPI data may attract more foreign investor buying of Polish T-bills," said Przemyslaw Manko, dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

Some dealers expected foreign investors, who bought 150 million zlotys of T-bills at this week's tender, to limit entry on Monday in order to place more bids at Thursday's 300 million zloty fixed bond tender.
"Foreign bids are likely to be divided between T-bills and fixed bonds next week," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

At Monday's T-bill auction the average yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill was seen down to around 21.33 percent from the previous 21.39 percent. The maximum yield was expected to form around 21.40 percent, dealers said.
The average yield of the 26-week paper may fall to around 21.36 percent from 21.39 percent and the shortest 13-week yield was seen falling to around 20.68 percent from 20.82 this week.
Dealers expected the zloty to drift between 2.35 and 2.5 percent from the parity rate next week without much impetus for either further gains or losses against the currency basket.

"The zloty will trade in the region of 2.5 percent from parity or slightly lower next week with possible foreign investor entry into Polish treasuries giving the local currency a boost," said Karol Zaluski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed the week around 2.45 percent from the central parity rate against last Friday's 2.51 percent close.
On the money market one-day rates were expected to increase to around 23 percent next week from Friday's 22 percent close when banks paid monthly taxes around Wednesday, dealers said.
